recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what you would do before squaring, and name the shape the locus turns out to be.
formula_note: PA + PB = const traces an ellipse; |PA − PB| = const traces a hyperbola for the same two foci — recognising ‘sum’ here separates this card from its difference-of-distances sibling in this unit. Both fixed points sit on the y-axis, so the ellipse's major axis lies along y with no shift to the centre.

steps.label: Take the locus point
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own. Both fixed points sit on the y-axis, symmetric about the origin, so the x-terms will cancel.
steps.memory_tip: Both fixed points sit on the Y-axis, so this time the x-terms are what cancel.

Mixing up which points are fixed and which one moves.

steps.label: Write the given condition
steps.margin_note: First mark. Isolate one distance, then square — squaring the sum of two roots directly leaves a cross term and needs a longer second squaring.
steps.memory_tip: ISOLATE one distance before squaring, so that only one root is left after the first squaring.

lines.text: (move PA² to the right and −12PB to the left)

recall.must_convey: That PA is isolated as 6 − PB and squared, giving 12PB = 36 + PB² − PA².

steps.why: Squaring PA + PB directly leaves a 2·PA·PB cross term. Isolating one distance first leaves only one square root, which the second squaring removes.
common_mistakes: Squaring PA + PB = 6 directly and being left with a cross term.

steps.label: Substitute the distances
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both fixed points have x = 0, so the x² terms are identical and cancel, and a difference of two squares in y finishes the line.
steps.memory_tip: Both have x = 0, so the x² terms are identical and cancel, leaving squares in y.

lines.text: (take out 4, then divide both sides by 4)

recall.must_convey: That the x² terms cancel and the difference of squares gives 3PB = 9 + 2y.
accept: the x squared terms cancel and the y difference of squares gives four a b

steps.why: PB² − PA² is a difference of two squares, so the y-terms simplify by (a+b)² − (a−b)² = 4ab and the line becomes first degree.
common_mistakes: Expanding both y-brackets fully and slipping a sign instead of cancelling.
Taking 4ab as 4(2)(y) but writing 8y² instead of 8y.

steps.label: Simplify to the locus
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. The 36y cancels across, 9y² − 4y² leaves 5y², and the constants give 45. Unequal positive coefficients again — an ellipse.
steps.memory_tip: Unequal but both POSITIVE coefficients — an ellipse.

steps.why: The locus of a point whose distances to two fixed points add to a constant greater than the distance between those points is an ellipse with those points as foci, so unequal positive coefficients on x² and y² are the expected finish.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that 36y appears on both sides and cancels.
Multiplying only x² by 9 and leaving the y-bracket alone.

insider_note: Isolate PA before squaring or a cross term is left. Both fixed points sit on the y-axis, so the x² terms cancel and (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab leaves 36 + 8y. The 36y then cancels on both sides.
